questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The junior clerk said, "I verify all digital case files diligently."

options.text: The junior clerk said that he verified all digital case files diligently.
The junior clerk told that he verified all digital case files diligently.
The junior clerk said that he verifies all digital case files diligently.
The junior clerk said that I verified all digital case files diligently.

questions.explanation: Past reporting verb 'said' ke sath Simple Present 'verify' Simple Past 'verified' mein backshift hoga. 1st person 'I' clerk (speaker) ke anusaar 'he' banega, aur conjunction 'that' quotation marks ko replace karega. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (C) mein tense backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (D) mein 'I' ko change nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01 & RC-06: Assertive Conversion & Simple Present Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The magistrate said to the witness, "You must speak the truth."

options.text: The magistrate told to the witness that he had to speak the truth.
The magistrate told the witness that he had to speak the truth.
The magistrate said the witness that he had to speak the truth.
The magistrate told the witness that you had to speak the truth.

questions.explanation: 'Said to the witness' convert hokar 'told the witness' banega (preposition 'to' ke bina). 2nd person 'You' listener 'the witness' ke anusaar 'he' banega. Obligation modal 'must' past reporting verb ke under 'had to' mein badlega. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein fatal 'told to' blunder hai. Option (C) mein 'said the witness' invalid syntax hai. Option (D) mein 'you' ko change nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02, RC-04 & RC-08: Said to ➔ Told & Must ➔ Had to.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The IT assistant said, "I am updating the High Court server patch now."

options.text: The IT assistant said that he was updating the High Court server patch then.
The IT assistant said that he is updating the High Court server patch now.
The IT assistant said that he was updating the High Court server patch now.
The IT assistant told that he had updated the High Court server patch then.

questions.explanation: Past reporting verb 'said' ke karan Present Continuous 'am updating' Past Continuous 'was updating' mein backshift hoga. 1st person 'I' assistant ke anusaar 'he' banega. Time adverbial 'now' shift hokar 'then' banega. Option (A) bilkul sahi hai. Option (B) mein backshift nahi hua. Option (C) mein 'now' ko retain rakha gaya. Option (D) mein continuous ko perfect bana diya gaya aur 'told' bina object ke hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06 & RC-10: Present Continuous ➔ Past Continuous & Now ➔ Then.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Present Perfect Backshift with Plural Speaker Pronoun
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The committee members said, "We have completed our investigation."

options.text: The committee members said that they have completed their investigation.
The committee members said that we had completed our investigation.
The committee members said that they had completed their investigation.
The committee members told that they had completed our investigation.

questions.explanation: Reporting subject 'The committee members' plural hai, isliye 1st person plural pronouns 'We' ➔ 'they' aur 'our' ➔ 'their' mein transform honge. Present Perfect 'have completed' past reporting verb ke under Past Perfect 'had completed' banega. Option (C) sabhi checks satisfy karta hai. Option (A) mein tense backshift missing hai. Option (B) mein pronouns unadjusted hain. Option (D) mein 'our' ko change nahi kiya gaya aur 'told' bina object ke hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03 & RC-06: 1st Person Plural Shift & Present Perfect ➔ Past Perfect.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Simple Past to Past Perfect Shift & Yesterday Adjustment
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The bench secretary said, "The registrar dispatched the judicial notice yesterday."

options.text: The bench secretary said that the registrar had dispatched the judicial notice the previous day.
The bench secretary said that the registrar dispatched the judicial notice yesterday.
The bench secretary said that the registrar dispatched the judicial notice the previous day.
The bench secretary told that the registrar has dispatched the judicial notice the day before.

questions.explanation: Simple Past 'dispatched' past reporting verb ke under Past Perfect 'had dispatched' mein backshift hoga. Time expression 'yesterday' shift hokar 'the previous day' banega. Option (A) bilkul flawless hai. Option (B) mein tense aur time dono ko chhod diya gaya. Option (C) mein Simple Past ko Simple Past hi rehne diya gaya (classic competitive exam trap). Option (D) mein 'has dispatched' aur 'told' bina object ke use hua hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07 & RC-10: Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect & Yesterday ➔ The previous day.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Past Continuous to Past Perfect Continuous Shift
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
Sunita said, "The audit officers were examining the accounts ledger."

options.text: Sunita said that the audit officers were examining the accounts ledger.
Sunita said that the audit officers had been examining the accounts ledger.
Sunita said that the audit officers had examined the accounts ledger.
Sunita told that the audit officers have been examining the accounts ledger.

questions.explanation: Past Continuous 'were examining' past reporting verb ke under Past Perfect Continuous 'had been examining' mein backshift hota hai. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (C) mein continuous aspect drop karke Past Perfect bana diya gaya. Option (D) mein Present Perfect Continuous laga diya gaya aur 'told' bina object ke use hua.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Past Continuous ➔ Past Perfect Continuous.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The Advocate General said, "The state government will issue the notification tomorrow."

options.text: The Advocate General said that the state government will issue the notification tomorrow.
The Advocate General said that the state government would issue the notification the following day.
The Advocate General said that the state government should issue the notification the following day.
The Advocate General told that the state government would issue the notification tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Future modal 'will' past reporting verb ke under 'would' mein backshift hota hai. Time expression 'tomorrow' shift hokar 'the following day' (ya 'the next day') banega. Option (B) dono rules ko perfectly apply karta hai. Option (A) mein koi change nahi hua. Option (C) mein 'should' lagakar meaning change kiya gaya. Option (D) mein 'tomorrow' ko unadjusted chhod diya gaya aur 'told' bina object ke hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08 & RC-10: Will ➔ Would & Tomorrow ➔ The following day.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
Naveen said to his assistant, "I can resolve this database issue."

options.text: Naveen told to his assistant that he could resolve that database issue.
Naveen told his assistant that he could resolve that database issue.
Naveen told his assistant that he can resolve this database issue.
Naveen said his assistant that he could resolve that database issue.

questions.explanation: 'Said to his assistant' ➔ 'told his assistant' (bina 'to' ke). 1st person 'I' Naveen ke anusaar 'he' banega. Modal 'can' ➔ 'could' banega. Demonstrative 'this' ➔ 'that' banega. Option (B) sabhi requirements ko accurately satisfy karta hai. Option (A) mein 'told to' blunder hai. Option (C) mein tense aur demonstrative shifts missing hain. Option (D) mein 'said his assistant' invalid syntax hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02, RC-08 & RC-10: Said to ➔ Told, Can ➔ Could, This ➔ That.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The clerk said, "The division bench may deliver the judgment on Friday."

options.text: The clerk said that the division bench might deliver the judgment on Friday.
The clerk said that the division bench may deliver the judgment on Friday.
The clerk told that the division bench might deliver the judgment on Friday.
The clerk said that the division bench must deliver the judgment on Friday.

questions.explanation: Past reporting verb 'said' ke karan modal 'may' ➔ 'might' mein backshift hoga. Quoted statement assertive hai, isliye conjunction 'that' aayega. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) mein backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (C) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (D) mein 'must' (compulsion) lagakar possibility ka original meaning corrupt kar diya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: May ➔ Might backshift with past reporting verb.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The advocate said, "I must file the urgent rejoinder today."

options.text: The advocate said that he must file the urgent rejoinder today.
The advocate said that he had to file the urgent rejoinder that day.
The advocate told that he had to file the urgent rejoinder that day.
The advocate said that he has to file the urgent rejoinder today.

questions.explanation: Specific deadline/obligation express karne wala modal 'must' past reporting verb ke under 'had to' mein badalta hai. 1st person 'I' advocate ke anusaar 'he' banega aur time expression 'today' shift hokar 'that day' banega. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein 'must' aur 'today' ko unadjusted chhod diya gaya. Option (C) mein 'told' bina listener object ke use kiya gaya hai. Option (D) mein 'has to' present tense aur 'today' laga diya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08 & RC-10: Must ➔ Had to & Today ➔ That day.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The physics teacher said, "Light travels in a straight line."

options.text: The physics teacher said that light traveled in a straight line.
The physics teacher said that light travels in a straight line.
The physics teacher told that light travels in a straight line.
The physics teacher said that light would travel in a straight line.

questions.explanation: 'Light travels in a straight line' ek eternal scientific truth (rectilinear propagation of light) hai. Scientific laws aur universal truths past reporting verb ke sath bhi Simple Present tense mein retain rehte hain (zero backshift). Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) over-backshifting error hai ('traveled' ka matlab hoga ki light ab straight line mein travel nahi karti). Option (C) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (D) modal distortion hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Scientific Law Exception to Tense Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The instructor said, "Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world."

options.text: The instructor said that Mount Everest was the highest mountain peak in the world.
The instructor said that Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world.
The instructor told that Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world.
The instructor said that Mount Everest had been the highest mountain peak in the world.

questions.explanation: Permanent geographical facts aur universal realities past reporting verb ke bawajood Simple Present tense mein uninflected rehti hain. Auxiliary 'is' freeze rahegi; 'was' likhna factual inaccuracy create karta hai. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) over-backshift trap hai. Option (C) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (D) Past Perfect distractor hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Permanent Geographical Fact Invariance.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The Chief Justice says, "The legal system exists to protect citizens' rights."

options.text: The Chief Justice says that the legal system existed to protect citizens' rights.
The Chief Justice said that the legal system existed to protect citizens' rights.
The Chief Justice says that the legal system exists to protect citizens' rights.
The Chief Justice told that the legal system exists to protect citizens' rights.

questions.explanation: Reporting verb 'says' Simple Present Tense mein hai. Rule: Jab reporting verb Present ya Future tense mein ho, toh reported speech ke tense mein ZERO backshift hota hai. Verb 'exists' Simple Present mein uninflected rahegi. Option (C) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein backshift kar diya gaya. Option (B) mein reporting verb ko hi past bana diya gaya. Option (D) mein 'told' bina object ke hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Present Reporting Verb ➔ Zero Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Future Reporting Verb ('Will say') — No Backshift
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The IT officer will say, "The network firewall is fully updated."

options.text: The IT officer will say that the network firewall was fully updated.
The IT officer will say that the network firewall is fully updated.
The IT officer would say that the network firewall was fully updated.
The IT officer will tell that the network firewall is fully updated.

questions.explanation: Reporting verb 'will say' Future Tense mein hai. Jab reporting verb future mein ho, toh reported speech ka tense bilkul change nahi hota. Auxiliary 'is' Simple Present mein retain rahegi. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein backshift kar diya gaya. Option (C) mein reporting aur reported dono verbs ko distort kiya gaya. Option (D) mein 'will tell' bina listener object ke use kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Future Reporting Verb ➔ Zero Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question: Which of the following indirect speech sentences is grammatically INCORRECT?

options.text: The registrar remarked that the court proceedings were being recorded digitally.
The advocate told to his junior that the hearing had been postponed.
The professor stated that honesty is the best policy.
The IT specialist said that the backup had completed two hours before.

questions.explanation: Sentence (B) grammatically incorrect hai kyunki yahan 'told to his junior' likha gaya hai. 'Tell' ek transitive verb hai jiske baad preposition 'to' lagana examination standard mein fatal blunder hota hai; correct form 'told his junior' hona chahiye. Baki sabhi options grammatically flawless hain: (A) mein 'remarked that' passive continuous ke sath valid hai, (C) proverb hone ke karan 'is' Simple Present mein freeze hai, aur (D) mein 'had completed' aur 'before' perfectly coordinated hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & Pitfall PIT-01: 'Told to + Object' Prepositional Blunder.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06
